items.headline: Guilfoyle resigns as ambassador to Greece at Trump's request
items.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as U.S. ambassador to Greece after the White House publicly asked her to step down. New press secretary Katie Zacharia announced the request at her first briefing, citing allegations that Guilfoyle sought $100,000 from a political donor to pay a personal credit card bill.

items.headline: Pope Leo has lung cancer, Vatican says after surgery
items.summary: The Vatican announced that Pope Leo XIV had surgery Tuesday to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. He had the lower lobe of his right lung removed.

items.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi oil sites in Yemen
items.summary: After deadly Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airports, a Saudi-led coalition struck oil facilities in Houthi-held Yemen. The escalation has raised fears of a wider regional war.

items.headline: Judge says Trump can't bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico
items.summary: A federal judge ruled that President Trump cannot bar news outlets from White House coverage because he dislikes their reporting. The ruling holds at least until a formal trial.

items.headline: Pakistan imposes emergency rule in Imran Khan's stronghold
items.summary: Pakistan declared emergency rule in the province governed by the party of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan. The NPR report describes the province as Khan's political stronghold.

items.headline: Congo's confirmed Ebola cases pass 9,000
items.summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo have surpassed 9,000 as containment efforts falter. Health workers are alarmed that many deaths are happening outside treatment centers.

items.headline: CVS to pay $315 million to settle opioid case
items.summary: CVS agreed to pay $315 million to settle a 2024 Justice Department lawsuit. The suit accused the pharmacy chain of dispensing excessive amounts of opioids and other controlled substances.

items.headline: Cornell halts fraternity parties after lawsuit
items.summary: Cornell is suspending social events at fraternity houses following a lawsuit by a student identified as Jane Doe. The university will also let state police investigate reported sexual assaults on campus.

items.headline: Poll: most Americans think Trump profits improperly from presidency
items.summary: A poll reported by TIME finds that most Americans believe President Trump is profiting from the presidency. Respondents described the profiting as illegal or unethical.

items.headline: Civil rights groups plan thousands of midterm poll observers
items.summary: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to polling places for the midterm elections. Political parties are also expanding monitoring, citing a charged political environment.

digest.overview:
Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as ambassador to Greece after the White House asked her to leave over allegations she sought $100,000 from a donor. A federal judge ruled President Trump cannot bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House coverage over their reporting, at least until a trial. The Supreme Court agreed to hear the administration's appeal in a watchdog's lawsuit seeking DOGE records. Treasury fined Bank of America more than $1.2 billion for anti-money-laundering and sanctions failures. JPMorgan's third-quarter earnings missed forecasts, while Citigroup and Wells Fargo beat them. CVS agreed to pay $315 million to settle a Justice Department case over opioid prescriptions. Cornell suspended fraternity parties and will let state police investigate reported sexual assaults.

Abroad, the Vatican said Pope Leo XIV had the lower lobe of his right lung removed in surgery that confirmed cancer. A Saudi-led coalition struck oil sites in Houthi-held Yemen, and a Houthi missile then caused a limited fire at an Aramco building in Dhahran with no casualties. A Russian missile hit a Kyiv power plant, killing at least two people despite Trump's claimed energy ceasefire, as Zelenskyy headed to London. Pakistan imposed emergency rule in the province run by jailed ex-prime minister Imran Khan's party. China and North Korea plan to open the long-idle New Yalu River Bridge to cargo on Thursday, and a stabbing in Incheon injured eight people. Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo passed 9,000. The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%.

home.overview:
The Rays evened the ALCS at 1–1 with a 3–1 win over Cleveland as Freddy Peralta struck out six and all three Tampa Bay runs came after a José Ramírez error; the series moves to Cleveland on Thursday. Milwaukee, up 2–0 in the NLCS, faces Blake Snell in Game 3 tonight at Dodger Stadium, where a banged-up Shohei Ohtani stays in the lineup despite a 3-for-20 postseason. In the NFL, Rams tackle Alaric Jackson drew a two-game suspension for punching Bradley Chubb, Bears pass rusher Montez Sweat got two games under the PED policy, and Dre Greenlaw lost his appeal. Week 6 starts Thursday with Seattle at Denver. NBA opening night is next Tuesday.

Barcelona won 4–1 at Galatasaray, Arsenal beat Lille 3–0 and Atlético beat Man United 2–0 in the Champions League, while Bayern were held 3–3 at Viking and Club Brugge won 4–3 at Inter. Man City host PSG and Roma host Real Madrid tonight. Championship leaders Swansea won 1–0 at Millwall in a game halted over alleged racist abuse, and Middlesbrough won 3–2 at Stoke. This weekend brings Real Betis vs Barcelona and Bayern vs RB Leipzig, plus K League title leaders FC Seoul hosting Gimcheon. In the KBO, LG and Doosan opened the postseason Wednesday in the wild card round at Jamsil.

brief: Seoul rivals LG and Doosan opened the postseason Wednesday evening with wild card Game 1 at Jamsil, with Carlos Carrasco starting for LG against Doosan's Gwak Been.
LG, the No. 4 seed, advance with a win or a tie, while No. 5 Doosan must win Game 1 and Thursday's Game 2.
The wild card winner visits No. 3 Kia in a best-of-five first round starting Saturday, with No. 2 Samsung waiting in the second round.
Regular-season champion KT Wiz open the Korean Series at home on Nov. 2.

brief: Freddy Peralta struck out six and the Rays beat the Guardians 3–1 to even the ALCS at 1–1, with all three Tampa Bay runs unearned after a José Ramírez error.
Liam Hicks' hit made it 3–0, Bryan Baker pitched a perfect ninth for his fourth save of the postseason, and Chase DeLauter's RBI double was Cleveland's only run.
Shohei Ohtani stays in the Dodgers lineup for NLCS Game 3 despite knee and biceps injuries and a 3-for-20 postseason, with Dave Roberts saying Ohtani is adamant he feels good enough.
Blake Snell starts Game 3 tonight at Dodger Stadium against Milwaukee's Robert Gasser, and Tyler Glasnow is set for Game 4 on Thursday.
The ALCS shifts to Cleveland for Games 3 and 4 on Thursday and Friday.
